assessment: The strongest public-administration response is academically credible: actual public policy, sustainability governance, constitutional/administrative law, public finance, organisational behaviour and empirical research are available. Description-only Public Policy Analysis is considered on its stated policy-process/memo content. The final decision is not a no-match caused by language or absence of a degree title. A current English target is contradicted by official identity evidence, so the former three Dutch-based UCR alternatives and all their placements are withdrawn from this target. No replacement schedules, speculative English curriculum or optional-research row are manufactured. CP220 remains the separate Dutch comparison.

GOSPOLI312.name: Public Policy Analysis
GOSPOLI312.content: Investigates public policy in the context of globalization. Uses a case study on sugar to examine policy‑making phases and alternative conceptualisations across national and international arenas. Students write policy memos.

ENSDELT312.name: Governance of Sustainability
ENSDELT312.content: Analyzes sustainability as a problem of collective decision-making involving governments, markets and civil society. Concepts of institutions, power, participation, justice and problem complexity frame competing technological and systemic responses. Structured cases examine food, freshwater, energy and climate mitigation. Students apply governance frameworks to a Zeeland issue, consult relevant organizations or experts, and produce policy advice or an evaluation assessing effectiveness, feasibility and stakeholder interests.

GOSLAWJ213.name: Comparative Constitutional Law
GOSLAWJ213.content: Compares constitutional structures, institutions and rights across legal systems and introduces administrative law. Students examine constitutional features, federalism, legislatures, executive relationships, courts, judicial review and human rights. The administrative component addresses public participation, remedies and procedural fairness. A staged booklet compares two constitutions, supported by legal interpretation, case-law analysis and application of principles to hypothetical facts.

BENECON311.name: Public Economics
BENECON311.content: Examines government intervention through the efficiency and equity effects of public policy. Market failure, public goods and externalities provide foundations for studying public production, collective choice, spending and taxation. Health, education, welfare and social insurance illustrate expenditure and redistribution questions. Students apply economic models, interpret data and graphs, evaluate research and develop a research proposal and paper.

BENLEAD311.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
BENLEAD311.content: Examines organizational behaviour at individual, group and organizational levels. Topics connect personality, perception, emotions and motivation to teams, leadership, power, conflict, structure, culture and change. Students design research plans for organizational cases and conduct a brief systematic literature review using PRISMA reporting tools. Workshops develop literature searching, study selection, source appraisal and synthesis, linking organizational-psychology evidence to practical questions and recommendations.

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.content: Develops qualitative inquiry from research design and preparation through data collection, management, analysis and dissemination. Students examine methodological foundations, ethics, positionality and reflexivity alongside interviews, focus groups, ethnography, documentary and visual approaches. Coding, thematic interpretation and NVivo support analysis. Research teams formulate a question, collect and analyze qualitative evidence, and report their methodological decisions, findings and limitations in staged assignments.
